notes.text: One manager owns the order, with one physical cup dispatched at a time. Its process scope and foreground service keep work independent of screen recreation.

The rulebook plans; it does not call hardware or write databases. It distinguishes payment approval, confirmed charges, drinks made, refunds and unknown outcomes. Conflicting evidence blocks unsafe work instead of replacing established truth.

The order, audit and outbox snapshot commit together before external commands run. A failed save blocks further work. On restart, uncertain in-flight work is retained as unknown—not blindly sent again.
The outbox is a queue for future uploads, not a working cloud connection. No uploader ships yet; this order loop runs locally.
The board supplies simulated evidence through the adapters. Both it and the kiosk read the same engine state; neither invents its own payment totals or drink outcomes.
Today these adapters charge no real money and move no real hardware. Release installs no order payment environment and leaves checkout unavailable.

The separate single-cup TCN path already exists, but a production OrderMachine bridge is not wired/qualified. It must reuse the single machine session; the machine controller—not this app—owns physical safety interlocks.

assumptions: This is the multi-cup order architecture we just hardened, not a diagram of every screen or the older single-cup vend implementation.
Numbered arrows describe each decision cycle, not a fixed payment sequence: prepaid-basket and per-cup-authorization flows use the same engine.
Demo administration, detailed threading and future backend integrations are omitted to keep the main responsibilities visible.
